title: Knobs on the sampler
summary: Temperature, top-k, top-p, repetition penalty, and constrained decoding.

choices.text: Top-k keeps the k largest logits and renormalizes. Top-p keeps the smallest set of tokens whose probabilities sum to at least p, so the shortlist grows when the distribution is flat and shrinks when it is peaked.
Temperature divides the logits before the softmax. Above 1 the distribution gets flatter. Toward 0 it approaches greedy argmax.
Greedy decoding and beam search both draw independent random samples, so running either of them twice gives different text.
A repetition penalty down-weights tokens that already appeared. It is a different control from temperature.
Constrained decoding masks any logit that would break a grammar or a schema, so the sample stays inside that language. Asking the model to "emit JSON" is a softer request, not the same guarantee.
